questions.q: List three modes of asexual reproduction with one organism each.
questions.a: Fission (amoeba), budding (yeast/hydra), fragmentation or spore formation (spirogyra, rhizopus).

questions.q: Why do offspring of asexual reproduction look like copies of the parent?
questions.a: Cells divide mitotically with little DNA variation, so offspring inherit nearly identical genetic material.

questions.q: Which is better for survival of a species over ages - asexual or sexual reproduction? Why?
questions.a: Sexual reproduction: it creates variations that help the species survive changing conditions.

questions.q: Name the parts of a carpel.
questions.a: Stigma (receives pollen), style (tube passage), ovary (holds ovules).
The pollen grain grows a pollen tube through the style carrying male gametes to the ovule.

questions.q: What do the ovule and ovary become after fertilisation?
questions.a: The ovule matures into a seed and the ovary into the fruit.

concepts.title: Human Reproductive System and Reproductive Health

questions.q: Name the organs that produce gametes in humans.
questions.a: Testes in males (sperms) and ovaries in females (eggs).

questions.q: What changes mark puberty in boys and girls?
questions.a: Boys: deeper voice, facial hair; girls: breast development, wider hips; both get pubic hair and faster growth.

questions.q: What is the role of the placenta?
questions.a: It supplies the foetus oxygen and nutrients from the mother's blood and removes wastes.
